dependency_inventory.description: Transport distance baseline test vector from the metric operator baseline test vector pack; currently VALID_METADATA_VECTOR only; expected transport distance fields not yet added.
The LP solver variant, pivot rule, and tie-breaking strategy must be declared before the test vector schema can be finalized. The baseline plan uses a fixed pivot rule for determinism.
The supply-demand balance tolerance (relative epsilon for sum(s) == sum(d)) must be declared before fixture schema can be finalized.
The canonical cost matrix representation format (JSON array of arrays of float64 values, row-major) must be declared before fixture schema can be defined.

determinism_requirements: For degenerate cases (m=1 or n=1) the transport distance is a closed-form weighted sum; it is fully deterministic given identical float64 inputs.
For general m x n balanced transport, the LP solver must be configured with a fixed pivot rule and declared traversal order so that equivalent problems always produce the same optimal transport plan.
The implementation plan must declare the LP solver variant, pivoting strategy, and tie-breaking rule before any implementation begins.
No randomized or probabilistic algorithm components are permitted in the baseline deterministic plan; stochastic LP variants are out of scope.
All transport distance computations must produce identical results across independent runs given identical inputs and an identical declared solver configuration.

implementation_prerequisites.description: MetricOperatorRank5SelectionPlan.v1 must be present selecting TRANSPORT at rank 5 with SELECTION_PLAN_ONLY scope.
MetricOperatorRank5CandidateAudit.v1 must be present confirming TRANSPORT as the rank-5 candidate.
TransportTestVectorSchemaPlan.v1 must be completed before fixture schema definitions can be created.
LP solver policy (solver variant, pivot rule, tie-breaking) must be declared in the implementation plan before any LP-dependent fixture values can be pinned.

implementation_risks.description: LP solver non-determinism for degenerate problems (multiple optimal transport plans): different pivot rules may yield different optimal T with the same objective value.
implementation_risks.mitigation: Declare a fixed, deterministic pivot rule and tie-breaking convention in the implementation plan; restrict test fixtures to problems with unique optimal transport plans until the tie-breaking policy is locked.

implementation_risks.description: Supply-demand balance floating-point drift: float64 summation of non-trivial supply/demand vectors may produce sum(s) != sum(d) at machine epsilon, triggering spurious NOT_COMPUTABLE.
implementation_risks.mitigation: Declare a relative balance tolerance (e.g., 1e-9) in the implementation plan; test fixtures must include a case near the tolerance boundary.

implementation_risks.description: Degenerate zero-supply/demand nodes: a supply or demand node with value 0.0 must not trigger division-by-zero in marginal constraint checking.
implementation_risks.mitigation: Add a dedicated NOT_COMPUTABLE or zero-marginal handling branch in the implementation plan; include a test fixture with a zero-supply node.

implementation_risks.description: Cost matrix size bounds: for large m, n, the LP has m*n variables; unbounded m and n may cause memory exhaustion.
implementation_risks.mitigation: Declare maximum allowed m and n in the implementation plan; add NOT_COMPUTABLE branch for oversized inputs.

input_shape_requirements: Supply vector s must be a non-empty sequence of non-negative finite float64 values; empty supply (m=0) must route to NOT_COMPUTABLE.
Demand vector d must be a non-empty sequence of non-negative finite float64 values; empty demand (n=0) must route to NOT_COMPUTABLE.
Cost matrix C must have shape (m, n) where m = len(s) and n = len(d); shape mismatch must route to NOT_COMPUTABLE.
All elements of C must be non-negative finite float64; negative or non-finite cost values must route to NOT_COMPUTABLE.
sum(s) must equal sum(d) to within float64 relative epsilon; unbalanced transport must route to NOT_COMPUTABLE.
Non-finite values (NaN, +Inf, -Inf) in s, d, or C must route to NOT_COMPUTABLE without any transport distance computation.
Negative values in s or d (individual supply/demand < 0) must route to NOT_COMPUTABLE even if the overall sum is non-negative.
mathematical_requirements: The discrete transport distance is defined over a finite set of source nodes with supply vector s ∈ R^m_+ and a finite set of target nodes with demand vector d ∈ R^n_+, paired with a cost matrix C ∈ R^{m×n}_+.
Balanced transport constraint: sum(s) must equal sum(d) to a tolerance of float64 epsilon; unbalanced inputs must route to NOT_COMPUTABLE.
The transport plan T ∈ R^{m×n}_+ minimizes the total cost sum_{i,j} C[i,j] * T[i,j] subject to the row marginal constraint T @ 1_n = s and the column marginal constraint T^T @ 1_m = d.
For the single-source degenerate case (m=1): T[0,j] = d[j] for all j; the transport distance is sum_j C[0,j] * d[j] with no LP required.
For the single-target degenerate case (n=1): T[i,0] = s[i] for all i; the transport distance is sum_i C[i,0] * s[i] with no LP required.
For the 1x1 degenerate case: transport distance equals C[0,0] * s[0] when s[0] == d[0]; otherwise NOT_COMPUTABLE.
When the cost matrix C is a valid metric distance matrix and supply/demand are probability simplices, the transport distance equals the discrete Wasserstein-1 distance with that ground metric.
All supply, demand, and cost values must be finite, non-negative float64; negative or non-finite values must route to NOT_COMPUTABLE.
numerical_constraints: Float64 precision required for all intermediate computations including cost accumulation, marginal constraint checking, and supply/demand balance.
Float32 is excluded from the baseline plan.
The balance check sum(s) == sum(d) must be performed in float64; the tolerance must be declared (e.g., relative epsilon 1e-9) before the implementation plan is finalized.
For large m or n, accumulated cost may approach float64 overflow bounds; the implementation plan must declare a bound on m, n, and cost values.
No transport distance computation of any kind is permitted during the planning phase.
numerical_stability_requirements: For degenerate m=1 or n=1 cases, cost accumulation uses left-to-right summation in declared index order; no reordering is permitted.
For general LP: dual variables (shadow prices) must be computed in float64 throughout; no intermediate float32 representation.
Degenerate LP solutions (multiple optimal transport plans) must be handled by a declared tie-breaking rule before implementation; the tie-breaking rule must be deterministic.
Zero-supply or zero-demand individual nodes (s[i]=0 or d[j]=0) are valid inputs; the implementation must handle zero-weight marginals without division by zero.
Very small positive supply/demand values (near float64 min positive) must not underflow to 0.0 in intermediate summations; a documented minimum value policy is required before implementation.

validation_requirements.description: Baseline test vectors must be extended with transport-specific reference inputs (supply vector, demand vector, cost matrix) and pinned expected transport distance scalars before implementation begins.
NOT_COMPUTABLE cases (unbalanced supply/demand, negative supply, negative demand, negative cost, empty supply, empty demand, non-finite values) must each have a dedicated validation fixture.
Deterministic replay validation: identical supply, demand, and cost matrix inputs must produce identical transport distance output across independent runs.
Float64 precision validation: all intermediate computations must use float64; no float32 intermediate values permitted.
Degenerate case validation: m=1 (single source) and n=1 (single target) must each have dedicated fixtures with analytically exact expected transport distance values.
